paragraphs: Friend, here's the big idea: you can hide a sin from a whole kingdom, but you can't hide it from the LORD. David acted in secret, and the LORD sent Nathan anyway. Notice HOW Nathan did it, though. He didn't come in swinging. He told a story that got David to see the truth with his own eyes, and then he said, "You are that man!" (2 Samuel 12:7).

Now here's the part I need you to hear. The moment David said, "I have sinned against the LORD," Nathan answered, "The LORD has taken away your sin" (2 Samuel 12:13). Friend, that is mercy, plain and simple. But the passage is honest too: forgiveness didn't erase every consequence, and David's household felt the weight of what he'd done (2 Samuel 12:10, 14). I think that's a hard thing to sit with, and it's worth sitting with. God forgives the sin, and it's still a serious thing.

And look where David goes when the worst news lands. He gets up, washes and goes into the house of the LORD and worships (2 Samuel 12:20). He pleaded while there was hope, and when the answer came, he turned toward God instead of away. Then the LORD loved the next child and gave him the name Jedidiah, "because the LORD loved him" (2 Samuel 12:25). So when you've blown it, baker, don't hide. Tell the truth, take it to the LORD, and keep walking toward Him, because the One who sees everything also forgives.
